references.text: The parallel text in the description of the priest's breastplate, where the third row of precious stones (leshem, shebo, and achlamah) is first prescribed by God to Moses.
The complete description of the breastplate with all twelve precious stones representing the twelve tribes of Israel, where verse 19 specifically mentions the third row.
The broader context for the making of the breastplate, where verse 12 is included as part of the description of how the craftsmen completed the work according to God's command.
Ezekiel's description of the precious stones in Eden's garden, which includes several of the same stones found on the priest's breastplate.
The description of the foundation stones of the new Jerusalem, which are adorned with precious stones and thematically connected to the twelve stones of the breastplate.
Prophetic foreshadowing and fulfillment: The earthly priesthood (the breastpiece) points forward to the foundation of the heavenly city.
